recent_papers.abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted mobile edge computing (MEC) is essential for supporting large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity; however, its performance is fundamentally constrained by fragmented optimization across the electromagnetic, network, and user behavior domains. This article proposes a holistic multidomain joint optimization framework that integrates these interdependent domains into a unified model, explicitly preserving the causal feedback chain from trajectory decisions through channel states to queue dynamics. The joint trajectory design, task offloading, and resource allocation problem is formulated as a mixed-integer nonconvex program (MINCP) to maximize long-term system utility. To solve this NP-hard problem, an iterative algorithm based on block coordinate descent (BCD) is developed, employing mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) and successive convex approximation (SCA) for tractable optimization. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework converges rapidly and exhibits superior robustness against environmental uncertainties via a maximin formulation. Notably, under heavy traffic loads, our method keeps task deadline violations below 2.5% while actively adapting the UAV trajectory to dynamic interference landscapes. This proactive coupling achieves up to a 23.5% reduction in total system energy consumption compared to conventional static-hovering baselines, thereby confirming the effectiveness of the cross-domain joint optimization paradigm.
